title: PSI-12 Predicting active and non-active corpus luteum in early pregnancy using computer vision and machine learning on Doppler ultrasound images in beef cattle.
content:
Abstract
Accurate assessment of corpus luteum (CL) functionality during early pregnancy is essential for reproductive management in beef cattle, particularly for resynchronization protocols to reduce the interval between inseminations and improve pregnancy rates. Doppler ultrasonography is commonly used to evaluate CL function by assessing blood perfusion, which is strongly correlated with progesterone secretion. Active CL displays greater vascularization, quantified through color Doppler imaging by measuring the proportion of blood flow within the luteal tissue. Reduced blood perfusion indicates functional luteolysis and non-active CL, linked to estrous return in non-pregnant cows. However, the subjective nature of visual assessment and inter-observer variability necessitate the development of automated, objective classification methods. This study aimed to develop and evaluate computer vision and machine learning models for the automated classification of active and non-active CL using Doppler ultrasound images in beef cattle. Doppler ultrasound videos of commercial Angus-Brangus cattle ovaries were collected as part of routine reproductive management and evaluated for blood flow. These videos were analyzed and classified by a panel of five experienced researchers based on criteria from the literature: non-active CL defined as having blood perfusion signals ≤ 25%, or a CL area < 2 cm². Accordingly, a dataset of active (n = 66) and non-active (n = 174) CL images was selected for evaluating our automated classification method using a four-step approach. In the first step, the dataset was randomly split into training (80%; active: n = 53; non-active: n = 144) and testing (20%; active: n = 13; non-active: n = 30) sets. In the second step, a deep learning-based Mask R-CNN computer vision model was trained to segment the images into CL tissue, anechoic structures within the CL tissue (if presented, e.g., CL cavity), and the background. If a cavity was detected, it was excluded from the tissue, leaving only the CL tissue for further analysis. In step 3, a threshold algorithm was applied to estimate the total area of blood flow in pixels and the percentage of blood relative to the CL tissue area. In the final step, a Random Forest model was trained using the extracted features from the training set to predict active and non-active CL in the testing set. Model performance was evaluated based on accuracy (0.96), precision (0.97), recall (0.94), and F1-score (0.95). These results highlight the potential of artificial intelligence to enhance early pregnancy diagnosis and reproductive efficiency in beef cattle. The integration of computer vision and machine learning techniques into ultrasound-based CL assessment provides a promising tool for improving reproductive decision-making and optimizing resynchronization strategies in commercial beef herds. This approach reduces the subjectivity inherent in manual analysis and could make the technology accessible by eliminating the need for highly trained ultrasound operators.
